stemMd: A block slides on a frictionless incline at 30 degrees to the horizontal. Using g=10 m/s squared, what is its acceleration down the incline?

options.label: C
options.textMd: 5 times the square root of 3 m/s squared

explanationMd: The parallel component of weight is mg sin30 degrees. Dividing by mass gives a=g sin30=10 times one half=5 m/s squared.

distractorRationale.d: The acceleration cannot exceed g in this simple model.
distractorRationale.a: Only the component parallel to the incline accelerates the block.
distractorRationale.c: This is the normal gravitational component's magnitude.
distractorRationale.e: Gravity has a nonzero component down the slope.
